example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, 13 weeks from Monday 6 October, cash floor $150,000. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Can you build our 13-week cash forecast? I need to know if we stay above our loan covenant.
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
Which horizon, from which start date? I propose 13 weeks.
Which accounts count as cash you can spend, and is any cash restricted? Please give me the bank balance of each on the start date, and the date of your last bank reconciliation.
What is your payroll calendar? I need the pay dates, net pay, tax deposit dates and benefit dates.
Which loan payments, tax due dates and other large one-off payments fall in the window?
Which open bills do you plan to pay, and when?
What is your cash floor? Is it a covenant or your own minimum, and how does it define cash?
Do you have a credit line? I need its limit, borrowing base and clean-down rules.
Is this one company, or several? If several, do you pool the cash?
Do you expect new sales in the window, or hold other currencies?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. 13 weeks from Monday 6 October. On 6 October the bank shows $151,900 in Operating and $30,500 in Savings. We reconciled both at 30 September. The Tax Reserve is restricted. Payroll, loan and tax dates are attached. We pay bills when due, but software and marketing can wait. The floor is a $150,000 covenant, cash net of restricted. One company, US dollars, no new sales to add.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I forecast **Northbrook Trading** for 13 weeks from **Monday 6 October**. Opening cash is Operating and Savings, without the Tax Reserve. I time each receipt from the customer's own payment history. Payroll, loans, taxes and the credit line come from your files. The floor is a **$150,000 covenant**, cash net of restricted. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Includes Harbor Retail and Meridian Foods
messages.summary: 13 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Week 1 opens with **$182,400** of cash you can spend. These are your bank balances on 6 October:
messages.after: I agreed both balances to the books through your 30 September bank reconciliation. The Tax Reserve holds $24,000 more. It is restricted, so I left it out.

messages.text: Here is the chain. Each week opens at the close of the week before. Each amount sits in the week the bank shows it.
messages.after: Only week 7 closes below your $150,000 floor. Cash stays above zero in all 13 weeks.

messages.text: Week 7 is your lowest point. It closes at **$131,000**, which is $19,000 below the covenant. Four payments land in the same week:
messages.after: I found the insurance renewal in last year's cash. No open bill covers it, so I count it once. You can still pay payroll. But a covenant breach can make the loan repayable at once.

messages.text: Two timing choices move cash between weeks. I place each amount in the week it reaches the bank, not on its due date:

messages.text: I also tested collections that arrive one week late. Then week 7 closes at **$135,600** and week 8 at **$146,900**. Two weeks break the floor instead of one.
These levers could fix week 7. Each one is a proposal for you. I do none of them.

messages.text: Your forecast has seven sheets. They are the 13 weeks, collections, payments, alerts, what-ifs, forecast against actual and coverage. The coverage sheet marks payroll, loan, tax and floor lines as supplied by you. Do you want the sheets as an Excel file?

Here is the workbook. It uses live formulas, so the chain changes when you change an input. Next week, give me the actual bank balances. I compare them with this forecast, drop week 1 and add a new week 13.
messages.after: Do you want me to save your settings for next week?

messages.text: Done. For Northbrook Trading, I saved the payroll calendar, the floor and its definition, the credit line terms and the lever list. I never save balances or the forecast.
